q: The surface that joins all the points of same phase is called ____.
e: A wavefront represents the continuous locus of points that are oscillating in unison.

q: When a series of wave strike an obstacle, they are ____.
e: This reversal of direction upon hitting a boundary is the fundamental nature of wave reflection.

q: This turning back of waves is called ____.
e: Reflection occurs when waves bounce off a barrier or obstacle.

q: When waves strike a ____, the waves are reflected from the barrier.
e: A straight barrier produces a predictable reflection where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

q: The angle of incidence is equal to the ____.
e: This is the law of reflection, which applies to all types of waves.

q: The wavelength and velocity of the wave remain ____ in reflection of wave.
e: Since the medium does not change during reflection, the wave's speed and wavelength are unaffected.

q: The speed of water waves depends on the ____.
e: Water wave velocity is directly influenced by the depth of the medium through which it travels.

q: It ____ when the depth of water becomes less deep.
e: Shallower water offers more resistance, causing the wave speed to drop.

q: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water the velocity of wave is ____ and the wavelength is shorter or vice-versa.
e: As velocity decreases in shallow water, the wavelength must also decrease to maintain a constant frequency.

q: When waves are incident to the boundary with an angle, the ____ of the waves changes.
e: A change in wave speed at a boundary causes the wave to bend, altering its direction of travel.

q: Such a change in direction is called ____.
e: Refraction is the bending of waves as they pass from one medium or depth to another.

q: It can be noticed that in refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but ____ remains the same.
e: Frequency is determined by the source and does not change when a wave enters a new medium.

q: Diffraction is the ____ from the straight-on direction through a gap (or) moves around an obstacle.
e: Diffraction describes how waves bend and spread out after passing through an opening or around a barrier.

q: The wave that passes the edges of the gap of the obstacle ____.
e: This spreading is the defining characteristic of wave diffraction.

q: The wider the gap, the ____ the waves spread out.
e: Diffraction is most pronounced when the gap size is comparable to the wavelength; a wider gap reduces this effect.

q: The narrower the gap, the ____ the waves spread out.
e: A narrower gap causes a greater degree of wave spreading due to increased diffraction.
